experiments.scope: Complete BLAKE3-r3 salted64-byte target, low12-bit walks. Sparse-checkpoint controller with m=2^(12/2), D=max(1,m/4096)=1, cap m+D; chronological and sorted checkpoint arrays. Every seed retained; seed-derived salt/start are reproducibility machinery, not ideal full-width coins.
experiments.hypothesis: Projected exact-target walks yield distinct-predecessor mask collisions under the checkpoint controller. D=1 does not exercise sparse gaps; this is not full-width probability evidence or a full256-bit collision witness.

experiments.scope: Complete BLAKE3-r3 salted64-byte target, low12-bit walks, checkpoint controller with m=2^(12/2), D=m/16, cap m+D. D=4 exercises nontrivial checkpoint gaps and local recovery. Seed salt/start reproducibility is not ideal full-width randomness.
experiments.hypothesis: The general sparse-gap checkpoint controller produces distinct-predecessor mask collisions at this finite width. Spacing ratio1/16 differs from full-width1/511; no full-width success probability follows.

experiments.scope: Complete BLAKE3-r3 salted64-byte target projected to low12 bits. m=2^(12/2), D=m/16; zero and indices at least m are omitted from search. q>=m is rejected. This matches the full attack endpoint pruning, but not its huge scale or spacing ratio.
experiments.hypothesis: Pruned checkpoint controller produces distinct predecessor mask collisions with actual full-attack insertion and recovery guards. Not full-width evidence, an iid success estimate or measured attack work.
